## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-sparse`:

$$
2^{O(k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Remove identically false constraints. If m ≥ q^r k, return YES by the uniform-assignment expectation bound; otherwise m=O_{q,r}(k).

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_{q,r}(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O_{q,r}(k)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $O_{q,r}(1)$ |

## Derivation

1. Every remaining constraint is satisfied with probability at least q^{-r} under a uniform assignment, so the preprocessing is valid. Only O(rm)=O_{q,r}(k) relevant variables remain.

2. Encode each finite-domain variable with one-hot bits, each local satisfaction indicator with a constant-size circuit, and the target number of satisfied constraints with a linear-size adder.

3. The full Boolean circuit and its counting-preserving gate encoding have O_{q,r}(k) variables and clauses. For this entry only the decision conclusion is used. Apply the sparse SAT bound.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- This is the absolute target, not an excess above the expectation or another guarantee.
- Weighted or succinctly compressed instances require separate size accounting.
- Examples include Max-Cut, Max-Dicut, fixed-width Max-SAT, and fixed-width Max-Lin2.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
